# MIntRec2.0

Observer-labeled communicative purposes in audiovisual TV dialogue, with 30 intent categories covering expressed attitudes and interpersonal goals. Labels describe portrayed social interaction, not the actors' private intentions.

## Example input and output

Author-published documentation example. It shows the data or task format, not a verified annotation row.

**Input:** An utterance's text, audio and speaker video within an ordered multi-party dialogue, with speaker identity.

**Output / label:** One of 30 intent labels (including Comfort and Ask for help) or the out-of-scope category; the official example image below shows labeled dialogue turns.

## Limits and notes

Included because labels represent human social and communicative purposes, rather than service-domain routing or slot filling. TV dialogue is scripted/performed and should not be described as unscripted natural behavior. Distinct from MIntRec: new taxonomy, dialogue context, speakers and out-of-scope data.
